input.story: I rented a room in Laxmi Nagar, Delhi for 11 months. Paid 20,000 deposit in cash to the owner, no rent agreement, only WhatsApp chats where he mentions "your deposit". Left on 30 Sept 2026. Now he doesn't pick up calls.

output.masked_story: I rented a room in Laxmi Nagar, Delhi for 11 months. Paid 20,000 deposit in cash to the owner, no rent agreement, only WhatsApp chats where he mentions "your deposit". Left on 30 Sept 2026. Now he doesn't pick up calls.

case.summary: The user rented a room in Laxmi Nagar, Delhi for 11 months, paid a cash security deposit of 20000 rupees, and left on 30 September 2026. The landlord is now unresponsive and has not returned the deposit.
case.user_goal: to recover the 20000 rupee security deposit

timeline.event: Moved into the room and paid 20000 deposit in cash
Vacated the room and attempted to contact landlord

evidence_missing: receipt or written acknowledgment of deposit payment
follow_up_questions: What was the exact date you moved into the room?
What is the landlord's full name or any contact details you have?
Do you have any written acknowledgment (message, receipt) that confirms the 20000 rupee deposit amount?
Did you receive any notice or statement about deductions from the deposit?

notes: Interest on delayed money may be claimable; the rate is for a lawyer/court to decide, so we don't add it here.

assessment.where_you_stand: You paid a cash security deposit of Rs 20,000 when you moved in on 30 Oct 2025 and vacated on 30 Sep 2026. The landlord has not returned the deposit and is not responding. You have WhatsApp chats showing the deposit was paid, but you lack a written receipt or rent agreement. Under contract law you can claim the amount you paid as compensation for the landlord’s breach [KB:ica_s73]. The deposit amount is within the usual cap and there is no evidence of lawful deductions, so you have a reasonable claim, though the missing written proof may be a weakness.

options.title: Send a polite written demand
options.what_to_do: Draft a short message/email stating the amount paid, request return of Rs 20,000 within 7 days, and mention you may take legal steps if not received. Attach screenshots of the WhatsApp chat as proof.
needs: WhatsApp screenshots, any chat where landlord acknowledges deposit

options.title: Legal notice through a lawyer
options.what_to_do: If no response, engage a lawyer to send a formal legal notice. The notice will cite breach of contract and demand payment within a reasonable period.
needs: WhatsApp screenshots, any written acknowledgment, copy of rent agreement if found

options.title: File a civil money recovery suit
options.what_to_do: Approach the Small Causes Court in Delhi and file a suit for recovery of Rs 20,000. Include the chat proof and a sworn statement. The claim is within the 3‑year limitation period [KB:deposit_civil_route].
options.time: 2‑4 weeks for filing, then months for hearing
needs: WhatsApp screenshots, affidavit, any rent agreement or receipt if available

proof_tips: Ask the landlord to confirm the deposit amount in writing (WhatsApp or email) and keep that message.
If you have any bank transfer or cash receipt slip, locate it; a handwritten receipt signed by the landlord is strong evidence.
Gather any photos of the room at move‑in and move‑out to show its condition.
what_i_dont_know: Exact wording of any tenancy law specific to Delhi that may affect the cap on deposits.
Whether the landlord ever gave a written acknowledgment of the deposit.
assessment.needs_lawyer_reason: The dispute is a simple monetary claim; you can start with a written demand and, if needed, a lawyer’s notice before going to court.
assessment.reply:
You paid a Rs 20,000 security deposit on 30 Oct 2025 and left the room on 30 Sep 2026. The landlord has not returned the money and is not replying. You have WhatsApp chats showing the payment, which lets you claim the full amount under contract law [KB:ica_s73]. Your main weakness is the lack of a written receipt or rent agreement. 

First, send a polite written demand (email or message) asking for the deposit back within 7 days and attach the chat screenshots. If there is no response, the next step is to have a lawyer send a formal legal notice. Should the landlord still ignore you, you can file a small‑claims suit in the Delhi Small Causes Court, which is still within the 3‑year limitation period [KB:deposit_civil_route]. 

Do you have any message where the landlord acknowledges receiving the Rs 20,000 deposit?
